subject: TYPE clause
notes: kb/Work PB1300. Rule (cite.py --check 13.18.57.4 'When the description of type-name-1 includes an implicit PICTURE clause derived from a VALUE clause, that implicit PICTURE clause becomes part of the description of the subject of the entry' -> OK §13.18.57.4 3)). SynthesizeImpliedPictures now runs BEFORE ExpandTypes over the written entries, so a template owns its SR9 PICTURE when the one description copy hands it over (with its provenance, DataItem.PicIsValueImplied): `01 U TYPEDEF VALUE "ABCD". 01 W TYPE U VALUE "Q".` gives W=[Q   ] LENGTH 4, V TYPE U gives [ABCD] 4, a group template member `05 M VALUE "XY"` reproduces as X(2) (R=[XY7] 3). First sentence: the subject's own literal initializes the composed item and is now screened against the composed description at ExpandType (§13.18.63.3 SR2/SR4 fire for `01 M TYPE N VALUE 12345` over PIC 9(3) and `01 Q TYPE P VALUE "ABCD"` over an explicit PIC X(2)). DETERMINATION: over an IMPLICIT template picture (`01 U2 TYPEDEF VALUE "AB". 01 W2 TYPE U2 VALUE "QRSTUV".`) no size rule applies - §13.18.63.3 SR4 bounds a literal by 'the size indicated by an explicit PICTURE clause' (cite.py OK §13.18.63.3 4)) - so W2 is X(2) holding [QR]; the adjudication's 'must reject' reading is rejected as ignoring the word 'explicit'.
